diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the supplementary statement, we use the preceding inequality on each of the finitely many connected components and sum over the latter.
\mathcal{R}(\Omega) \coloneqq \operatorname{ker} \BD =  \{\bx \mapsto A\bx + \bb \text{ for some } A \in \setR^{d \times d} \text{ with } A = -A^\top \text{ and } \bb \in \setR^d \}.
\bv \mapsto \norm{\bv \cdot \bn}_{L^q(\Gamma)}\qquad \text{is a norm on the  rigid deformations $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$}

issues.failure_explanation: For a disconnected domain, ker(BD) consists of fields that are rigid on each connected component independently, while the paper identifies the rigid deformations with the globally affine fields Ax+b (valid only for connected Omega). Assumption assump:dom for such Omega only detects global rigid fields, and the proof of the supplementary statement applies the connected-case inequality componentwise, which would require the normal-trace seminorm to be a norm on each component's own rigid fields -- not implied by the hypotheses. Counterexample (d=2): Omega = union of two disjoint balls, Gamma = partialOmega. Any globally affine skew field rho = Ax+b with rho·n = 0 on Gamma must satisfy b = Ax_1 = Ax_2 and A(x_1-x_2)=0, hence A=b=0, so Assumption assump:dom holds; but the field equal to the rotation x -> A(x-x_1) on the first ball and 0 on the second lies in ker(BD), has tr(rho).n = 0 on Gamma and positive W^{1,p}-norm, contradicting eq:kornetto0.

failure_location.quote: The same conclusion holds true if $\Omega\subset\R^{d}$ is open and bounded with Lipschitz boundary and has finitely many connected components.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to the supplementary statement the hypothesis that the normal-trace seminorm is a norm on the rigid fields of each connected component (i.e., Assumption assump:dom per component, with respect to the piecewise-rigid kernel); then apply the connected-case inequality on each component and sum.
issues.overall_effect: The supplementary statement of Theorem thm:korn-n (finitely many connected components) is false as stated. Nothing else in the paper invokes the multi-component case (all applications use connected polyhedral domains), so no other labelled result is affected.
issues.title: Supplementary Korn inequality for domains with several connected components is false
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis (per-component non-degeneracy) restores the supplementary statement by the very same componentwise argument; every advertised claim of the paper (connected polyhedral domains) is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and suppose that $\pi(x)\coloneqq Ax+b$ satisfies $\pi=0$ on $\Gamma$, whereby $\pi=0$ on $H_{1}\cup H_{2}$.
\bv \mapsto \norm{\bv \cdot \bn}_{L^q(\Gamma)}\qquad \text{is a norm on the  rigid deformations $\mathcal{R}(\Omega)$}

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption assump:dom requires that a rigid field rho = Ax+b with rho . n = 0 on Gamma vanish. The proof instead supposes that the full field pi = Ax+b vanishes identically on Gamma, a strictly stronger premise that is not available. Under the correct premise one only obtains A*nu_i = 0 and (A*xi_i+b)*nu_i = 0 for the two non-collinear normals, which does not determine A and b when d >= 3. Counterexample (d=3): Omega = (0,1)^3, Gamma_1 = the face {x_1=0}, Gamma_2 = the face {x_2=0} (both of positive H^2-measure, contained in hyperplanes with normals nu_1 = e_1, nu_2 = e_2, non-collinear). The rigid deformation rho = e_3 (A=0, b=e_3) satisfies rho . n = 0 on Gamma = Gamma_1 u Gamma_2 but rho is nonzero; hence v |-> ||v . n||_{L^q(Gamma)} is not a norm on R(Omega) and the conclusion fails. (In d = 2 the statement is true.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the criterion by a spanning condition: assume that the unit normals attained on Gamma_1 u Gamma_2 span R^d (for Gamma = partial Omega of a bounded polyhedron this holds automatically), and redo the elementary verification with the correct premise pi . n = 0 on Gamma, which yields A*nu_i = 0 and b·nu_i = 0 for a spanning family of normals, hence A = 0 and b = 0.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised geometric criterion (two non-collinear normals on Gamma suffice) is false in dimension d = 3, so Assumption assump:dom is not verified by Corollary cor:polyhedral in the stated generality; the discussion of mixed boundary conditions (Remark rmk:mixed-bc) and the caption of Figure fig:Korno lose their support. The main theorems use Gamma = partial Omega of a polyhedral domain, where the norm property holds by the direct (unwritten) argument in Lemma lem:h-norm, so the main convergence results are not invalidated.
issues.title: Corollary cor:polyhedral: two non-collinear face normals do not make Assumption assump:dom hold in d = 3
issues.why_classification: The stated criterion is false and must be weakened, withdrawing a substantive geometric promise; the corrected statement is elementary but changes the advertised result, and the main convergence theorems survive via the separate full-boundary argument, so the loss is contained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Raising both sides to the power $\frac{8}{d+4}$, summing over $j$ and multiplying by $\delta_k^2$

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:p-est only provides the delta_k^2-weighted bound delta_k^2 sum_j ||pi^k_j||_{L^2}^{p} <= c with p = 8/(d+4), i.e. ||pi^k||_{L^p(I;L^2)}^p = delta_k sum_j ||pi^k_j||^p <= c/delta_k. Since xi^k(t) = int_0^t pi^k(s) ds, Hardy/Young estimates only yield ||xi^k||_{L^p(I;L^2)} <= C ||pi^k||_{L^p(I;L^2)} <= C delta_k^{-1/p}, which diverges; indeed a single time step with ||pi^k_{j0}|| ~ delta_k^{-2/p} is compatible with Lemma lem:p-est and drives ||xi^k||_{L^p(I;L^2)} to infinity. The uniform bound eq:est-press-4, on which the weak compactness of (xi^k) and the entire limit passage in the pressure term rest, is therefore not established by the cited estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Sum the discrete momentum identity over i <= j to get an equation for xi^k_j = delta_k sum_{i<=j} pi^k_i, test it via the discrete inf-sup condition against bv_h in X_h cap H^1_0, and bound the right-hand side using the telescoping identity (difft bu^k_i, bv_h)_B delta_k-summed = (bu^k_j - bu^k_0, bv_h)_B together with the already established bounds (Lemma lem:apriori-unst and the estimates in the proof of Lemma lem:p-est). This yields sup_t ||xi^k(t)||_{L^2(Omega)} <= c uniformly in k, which implies eq:est-press-4; the remainder of the proof of Lemma lem:unst-conv-pi applies unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The weak compactness of (xi^k) in L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2(Omega)), the convergence of the pressure pairings in Lemma lem:unst-conv-pi, and consequently the derivation of the distributional and pressure-free limit formulations in Proposition prop:limit-eq (and hence the convergence statements of Theorems thm:main-unsteady and thm:main-unsteady-v) are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Uniform bound for the pressure primitive xi^k is not derived from the discrete pressure estimate
issues.why_classification: The gap is closed by a short, routine estimate using only tools and bounds already proved in the paper (telescoping in time plus the discrete inf-sup condition); no new lemma, construction or weakening is needed and every conclusion and rate is preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: While in space we have full admissibility, in time some integrability is missing due to the convective term.
Then, first taking the limit in $\oldepsilon \to 0$, and then $\delta \to 0$ one can show that the energy identity is satisfied for a.e. $0 < s_1 < s_2 < T$.
This can be derived by the energy identity in Proposition~\ref{prop:limit-eq} and the corresponding energy inequality for $\bu^k$.

From the exponents we see that admissibility of 
a solution as test function 
is lost in dimension $d = 3$.
Due to the convective term, the velocity function is not an admissible test function for the three dimensional time-dependent Navier--Stokes equations.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 4 of the proof tests the limit formulation with bu_{epsilon,delta} in C(Ibar; W_div) and claims the energy identity. In dimension d = 3 the trilinear form is only controlled with the third argument in L^{8/(4-d)}(I;H^1) = L^8(I;H^1) (cf. eq:conv-id/est:conv-t-a1), and the paper itself states that 'admissibility of a solution as test function is lost in dimension d = 3' and that 'only an energy inequality rather than an equality is available'. Truncation and mollification in time do not repair this: the convective term int_Q (bu otimes bu):grad bu_{eps,delta} requires time integrability of grad bu_{epsilon,delta} beyond L^2(I;L^2) (time mollification of an L^2-in-time field carries constants that blow up as the mollifier degenerates), so neither the term nor its convergence is justified in d = 3. Moreover, the limit passage from the discrete level can only produce an energy inequality, since the dissipation of bu^k is controlled only in the liminf sense; the equality cannot be recovered from the available compactness. Lemma lem:unst-conv-s-c2-v explicitly derives the Minty hypothesis est:minty-lsc-claim from this identity, so the identification of the nonlinear boundary relation for r > 2 -- and with it Theorem thm:main-unsteady-v, whose point is exactly the regime r in (2,2^sharp) -- is unsupported. (In d = 2 the velocity is admissible and the identity is fine.)

failure_location.quote: is satisfied for a.e. $0<s_1<s_2< T$, and for $s_1 = 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either prove the energy equality for the constructed limit in d = 3 (which the source's own admissibility analysis indicates is unavailable for weak solutions of the 3D Navier--Stokes system) or replace the derivation of the limsup condition est:minty-lsc-claim in Lemma lem:unst-conv-s-c2-v by an argument requiring only the energy inequality; otherwise the convergence claim for r in (2,2^sharp) must be restricted to d = 2, excluding an advertised regime.
issues.overall_effect: The energy identity claimed in Proposition prop:limit-eq is unsupported in dimension d = 3 (only an energy inequality is derivable), and consequently the Minty-type identification of the boundary relation and the convergence/existence result of Theorem thm:main-unsteady-v for r in (2,2^sharp) in dimension d = 3 -- the entire point of Section sec:asym-Nitsche -- are unproven. The r <= 2 theory (Theorem thm:main-unsteady), which uses strong trace convergence instead, is not affected.
issues.title: Energy identity of the limit solution is not established in d = 3; Minty identification for r > 2 breaks down
issues.why_classification: Every supported resolution requires essentially new proof architecture (an energy-equality mechanism for 3D weak solutions, or a genuinely different Minty-type argument); otherwise the advertised d = 3, r in (2,2^sharp) regime must be abandoned, which is a major loss for the primary result of Section sec:asym-Nitsche.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let Assumption~\ref{assump:cases}~\ref{itm:case-impl-coerc} be satisfied, and let $\lambda\geq 0$, $\alpha>0$ be such that Assumption~\ref{as:param-v} holds and let $r \in (2,2^\sharp)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:main-unsteady-v allows any alpha > 0 (Assumption as:param-v constrains only lambda), and its proof asserts that the a priori estimates carry over 'verbatim' from the symmetric method. In the antisymmetric scheme the quadratic part is 2 nu ||BD v||^2 + nu alpha ||h^{-1/2} v.n||^2 (no cross term), while the boundary term contributes -lambda ||tr_tau v||^2_{L^2(Gamma)}, which in the proof of Lemma lem:apriori-unst (est:unst-ap-5) is absorbed against the Nitsche-controlled ||.||_{X_h}-term; that absorption requires nu min(2,alpha) > lambda c^2_tr,K, which for alpha < 2 is not implied by Assumption as:param-v. Hence for small alpha and positive lambda the a priori estimate eq:Tabowser -- and with it the Brouwer fixed-point argument for the existence of discrete solutions -- is not established under the stated hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: From this, it follows that Lemma~\ref{lem:apriori-unst}, \ref{lem:ex}, \ref{lem:dt-est}, \ref{lem:p-est}, \ref{lem:unst-conv-u}, \ref{lem:unst-conv-pi} and Proposition~\ref{prop:limit-eq} hold verbatim, without the assumption on $\alpha$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the coercive part of the boundary term instead of discarding it: use <Seps(tr_tau v), tr_tau v>_Gamma >= c(||Seps||^{r'} + ||tr_tau v||^r - 1) (already displayed in est:unst-ap-5a, valid since r > 2) and absorb -lambda||tr_tau v||^2_{L^2} into c||tr_tau v||^r_{L^r} via Young's inequality; the Nitsche quadratic part is nonnegative for every alpha > 0, yielding eq:Tabowser and the existence of discrete solutions with no condition on alpha.
issues.overall_effect: Under the stated hypotheses the uniform bound eq:Tabowser and the existence of discrete solutions for the antisymmetric scheme are unproven, so the existence part of Theorem thm:main-unsteady-v is unsupported as written. The conclusion itself is recoverable, so no downstream result is lost beyond the present gap.
issues.title: A priori estimates for the antisymmetric Nitsche method are not justified without a condition on alpha
issues.why_classification: A one-line absorption using the coercivity estimate already displayed in the paper (est:unst-ap-5a, valid since r > 2) repairs the gap; every statement, rate and guarantee of Theorem thm:main-unsteady-v is preserved.
